title: Casper and the Ember
premise: Odile Eriksen, once a battle-priest of the silent god Vael, has hidden for a decade as a charm-seller in the magic-outlawed city of Greyhollow. When Casper, a feral child speaking the dead tongue of the old gods, arrives at her door, Odile learns the boy is an ember of Vael's scattered divinity—and that King Aldric has been hollowed out and worn as a vessel by the god-devourer Mauveth, who hunts the remaining embers to finish consuming Vael entirely. Pursued by the king's witch-finders, Odile and Casper flee to the drowned temple where she was first sworn, discovering along the way that her own silence-broken faith was never abandonment but a test she failed by hiding. In the temple, Odile chooses to pour her ten years of hoarded, unspent devotion into Casper rather than claim the power herself, reigniting Vael long enough to burn Mauveth out of Aldric; the god goes silent again, but this time by choice, leaving its embers free. Odile takes Casper not as a weapon or a ward, but as family, and together they walk back into a city that will have to learn what magic, freely given, can be.
about_author: Rafael Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing defunct religious orders before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about faith, bureaucracy, and the people who fall through the cracks of both.

chapters.title: The Child Who Spoke First
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Selling charms under a false name in Greyhollow, Odile recognizes the danger when witch-finders begin sweeping the market—and then finds Casper on her doorstep at midnight, speaking the pre-kingdom liturgical tongue she swore she'd never answer. The emotional beat: terror curdling into reluctant recognition, as the child calls her by her true name, Eriksen-of-the-Ninth-Vow.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Odile and King Aldric. Fleeing the city with Casper, Odile deciphers the boy's words: he is an ember of the silent god, and something ancient is eating the others. In the palace, we see Aldric dimly aware he is a passenger in his own body as Mauveth turns the witch-finders toward the child. Emotional beat: dread and dawning responsibility—Odile realizes hiding made her complicit.

chapters.title: The Drowned Temple
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the flooded ruins where she took her vows, Mauveth's forces corner them, and Casper begins to burn out from the divine power he cannot contain. Mauveth offers Odile restoration of her lost standing if she surrenders the boy. Emotional beat: the climax of temptation—power offered to someone who learned to want nothing—and her choice to give everything instead.

chapters.title: Ember, Unbound
chapters.summary: Shared POV, shifting between Odile and Casper. Odile pours her decade of hoarded devotion into Casper, reigniting Vael, which burns Mauveth out of Aldric and then deliberately goes quiet, freeing its embers. Aldric wakes in his own body; the witch-finders scatter without their master. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—belonging chosen rather than granted—as Odile and Casper walk home through a changed city.
